title: Platform all-hands heatmap & dependency notes — Jul 21 2026
content:
(Meeting started 10:00am) Quick pulse and a heatmap walkthrough. Note: informal capture — action owners assigned during the call.

Agenda:
- 10m: Quick metrics pulse (latency, error-rate, capacity)
- 20m: Heatmap review — hot endpoints & model-variant pressure
- 15m: Cross-team dependency block review
- 15m: Triage and assign action items
- Parking lot / follow-ups

Heatmap snapshot (observability view):
- Highest token-per-second pressure: /v1/generate for gpt-redwood-small at 1.2M tps/day — unusual spike from a single key (growth-test-app-3). Linked to PLAT-482.
- Latency tails: p95 increased from 320ms -> 410ms for short requests (<128 tokens) on recently deployed batcher-optimizer 2.1. Suspect kernel selection fallback on A100p nodes.
- KV cache hit rate steady at 72% overall; two customer routes (enterprise/sales-demo and dedicated/customer-A) showing <40% due to sequence variance.

Quick metrics (top-of-mind):
- Platform SLO: 99.5% reqs < 500ms — current week 99.1% (regression vs last week). Root-cause candidates: model routing and hot-key bursts.
- Error budget: ~3.2% remaining for monthly window (alerting threshold set at 2.0%).
- Dedicated pool utilization: avg 68% across clusters; one cluster (eu-west-2-dedicated-3) at 91% — risk of queueing.

Highlights & Incidents discussed:
- Growth-test-app-3 identified as noisy key; mitigation: temporary rate-limiting and re-route to lower-cost variant (gpt-redwood-mini) — action: Miguel -> implement policy by 7/22.
- Batcher-optimizer 2.1 rollback considered; current plan: enable stricter kernel pinning in canary nodes and redeploy patches (PR: github.com/.../runtime/pull/1276) — action: Lin -> coordinate rollout, target 7/23.
- KV cache regression for sales-demo: suspected prompt prefix entropy. Solution: add adaptive prefix grouping in cache policy; prototype by 7/29 — action: Elena.

Cross-team dependency map (quick list):
- Serving-runtime needs PR for kernel selection to accept model-hint header (blocking platform rollout) — blocker for 2.1 fixes. Blocked-by: runtime team (Lin).
- Console/rollouts needs feature flag support for temporary rate-limit rules exposed via API (for ops) — owner: product (Rajiv) to scope next sprint.
- SRE to provision temporary additional Dedicated capacity in eu-west-2 while migration occurs (ticket created: PLAT-495) — owner: Chris -> follow-up with infra.

Action items (concise):
- Miguel Ramirez: implement short-term policy to re-route noisy API key -> complete by 2026-07-22. Linked PR/notes: confluence:policy/noisy-key-7-22.
- Lin Chen: coordinate kernel pinning canary + patch; validate p95 regression fixes; complete canary by 2026-07-23.
- Elena Morris: prototype adaptive prefix grouping for KV cache; results on test set due 2026-07-29.
- Rajiv Kapoor (product): add feature-flagging scope for runtime rate-limit toggles; sync with devtools by 2026-07-26.
- Chris O'Neill: open capacity runbook and request extra Dedicated nodes for eu-west-2; update ticket PLAT-495 by 2026-07-22.
- All: add test prompts to observability evals dashboard (owner: Asha) by 7/24 — short checklist: add 50 prompts, include sales-demo & growth-test-app cases.

Decisions made:
- No full rollback of batcher-optimizer 2.1 yet; prefer targeted kernel pinning + canary expansion.
- Short-term noisy-key throttling allowed for growth-testing; implement as temporary policy tied to audit log.

Risks & open questions:
- If kernel pinning slows down throughput on other models, we may need a staged opt-in for top-volume customers. How to communicate? (Product/CS)
- Are there regulatory implications of re-routing enterprise traffic to lower variants? (Legal/Compliance check requested)

Notes-to-self / informal:
- Need one-pager for execs on "heatmap signal -> mitigation flow" (for finance + sales). Draft after actions trimmed.
- Slack thread #platform-ops: ref 07/21 'heatmap spike' has more raw logs. Tagging Miguel to add summary.

Parking lot:
- Explore autopruning of cold prefixes from KV cache to reclaim memory (low priority).
- Evaluate model-variant fallback economics next quarter (cost vs latency trade-offs).

Next all-hands check: propose follow-up sync Fri 2026-07-23 10:00 for quick status; full review at next org-wide all-hands in two weeks.

Raw links mentioned during meeting:
- Jira: PLAT-482 (noisy-key), PLAT-495 (capacity request)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1276
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PLAT/pages/heatmap-signal-flow-jul2026

End notes: captured by Asha Patel — rough draft, please add corrections inline.
